modelingDirection: Minimum details are native voxels; continuous garment panels, slopes, cavities and straps. Rigid joints transform vertices without resampling.

tests.fullRegressionScope: 401 tests on the final M038 geometry; a subsequent correction replaces nominal recipe lookup dimensions with actual default posed extents and adds a consistency assertion, then reruns all eight focused tests and the build. Geometry hashes and exports remain unchanged.

visualReview.method: Inspected real final editor screenshots, using 2x2 scene contact sheets and two underside contact sheets, plus full-size parameter rebuild detail views. No scratch image is relabelled as a final render.
findings: Three long garments have distinct hem/sleeve/trim silhouettes; skin, hair and hands are actual retained sources. Visible rigid shoulder seams remain.
Rain membrane is transparent in the material view; clay/front views intentionally show opaque surfaces. Hood face opening and open-sided cape remain legible.
Scarf neck ring, separate rescue foam blocks, pilot fleece edges, bandage bands and right-leg brace hardware are visible.

Both bag covers visibly open off the body; cavities are real. Closed bag scenes use actual adults. Shoulder straps remain rigid, angular and visibly spaced from parts of the torso; these require aesthetic refinement.
Adult and child gloves retain separately sized hands and both reflected sides; palm/thumb web remains simplified and bulky. Wrist opening and closed finger tips are visible.
Small buckles, woven marks, fringe and protective blocks retain voxel detail; clothing and straps show continuous sloped and curved faces.

Final atlas and material comparison frame all twelve actual masters; the wear overview uses material views so rain transparency is visible. Surface ornament, tailoring density and anatomical detail are simpler than the reference.
limitations: Assistant visual inspection is not human art acceptance or reference-fidelity approval.
No full dynamic cloth, grip, arbitrary pose or gameplay acceptance.
Technical fit audits are finite checks; visual review does not replace geometry evidence.

developmentCorrections: Rounded rectangular robe hips around retained trousers; elevated the wedding front inset above shoes.
Rain hood expanded around actual CHAR085 hair, with a true face opening.
Glove palm and proximal thumb share a rigid cavity; shortened proximal finger walls to the visible palm edge; wrist buckle seats outside the actual child skin. Original CHAR070 retained.
Actual CHAR113/118 underlayers replace both old body shirt and trousers. Limb brace follows real CHAR118 leg profiles.
Backpack straps route outside body and trouser surfaces. Both bags use a forward-opening prop hinge, with moving cover/handle/roll and fixed front panel, avoiding fixed straps at eight named angles.
limitations: Technical candidates; human art acceptance zero.
Original actor source, size matrix, protected clearance and original skeleton/controllers are unavailable.
Body pieces standing only; gloves open-hand only. Rigid per-component skinning, no soft cloth, IK or animation clips.
Closed bags author adultA only; open variants off body. Eight sampled lid angles do not certify every continuous movement. Intentional hinge axle contact is named and excluded.
Bandage body skin derives from clothed author profiles. Proximal thumb shares the palm shell; no full thumb-flexion claim.
Visible rigid shoulder seams, simplified palm shell and fixed straps remain for art review.
Triangle sampling and edge tests are not a formal all-motion certificate.
Rain alpha, foam, braces and optics do not imply waterproofing, flotation, medical behavior, safety certification or bound equipment power.
Software WebGL is not hardware frame-rate acceptance.
